title: Disruption of CD91 association with AXL and Fgr abrogates HSP-mediated signaling and cancer immunosurveillance.
authors: Harkness, Trey; Sedlacek, Abigail L; Shah, Keya; Juergens, Alyssa M; Greenberger, Joel; Mukherjee, Amitava; Binder, Robert J
one_liner_zh: 该文研究CD91受体与Fgr/AXL的蛋白-蛋白相互作用及肿瘤免疫监视信号，虽用AlphaFold预测结合区域，但对象为受体-激酶互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: CD91 serves as a receptor that causes the activation of antigen-presenting cells in response to cancer cells by binding HSPs. In this context, the HSP-CD91 axis is responsible for the rejection of emerging and nascent cancers. The role of CD91 in the cross-presentation of HSP-chaperoned peptides is well established, but its contribution to cell signaling and costimulation is less clear. We investigated CD91-mediated signaling with respect to cancer immunosurveillance by examining two key adaptor proteins, Fgr and AXL. To investigate the interactions between the beta chain of CD91 and Fgr and AXL, AlphaFold was used to predict protein‒protein binding areas. Signaling was further investigated by examining NF-kappaB phosphorylation and cytokine production in iBMDMs with CRISPR-induced tyrosine mutations. Mice conditionally lacking Fgr and AXL in dendritic cells were assessed for their ability to control tumors in inducible and transplantable models of cancer. In silico or CRISPR-mediated disruption of key tyrosines within CD91 abrogates Fgr binding, NF-kappaB activation, and cytokine release. Using a DC-specific Fgr knockout mouse model, we revealed that loss of Fgr severely impaired tumor immunosurveillance, whereas AXL knockout resulted in a milder phenotype, suggesting a greater downstream role. Loss of Fgr also prevents the development of adaptive immunity to tumors following HSP immunization, but it has no impact on transplantable tumor growth. These findings elucidate key components of the CD91 signaling mechanism, advancing our understanding of how dying tumor cells initiate adaptive immune responses and providing a therapeutic target to enhance this pathway.
abstract_zh: CD91作为一种受体，通过结合HSPs（热休克蛋白）响应癌细胞，从而激活抗原呈递细胞。在此背景下，HSP-CD91轴负责排斥新生和早期癌症。CD91在HSP伴侣肽交叉呈递中的作用已得到充分证实，但其在细胞信号传导和共刺激中的贡献尚不明确。我们通过研究两个关键衔接蛋白Fgr和AXL，探讨了CD91介导的信号传导在癌症免疫监视中的作用。为研究CD91β链与Fgr和AXL之间的相互作用，使用AlphaFold预测蛋白质-蛋白质结合区域。通过检查CRISPR诱导酪氨酸突变的iBMDMs中NF-kappaB磷酸化和细胞因子产生，进一步研究了信号传导。在诱导性和移植性癌症模型中，评估了树突状细胞中条件性缺失Fgr和AXL的小鼠控制肿瘤的能力。计算机模拟或CRISPR介导的CD91关键酪氨酸破坏消除了Fgr结合、NF-kappaB激活和细胞因子释放。使用DC特异性Fgr敲除小鼠模型，我们发现Fgr缺失严重损害肿瘤免疫监视，而AXL敲除导致较温和的表型，表明其下游作用更大。Fgr缺失还阻止了HSP免疫后对肿瘤的适应性免疫发展，但对移植性肿瘤生长无影响。这些发现阐明了CD91信号传导机制的关键组成部分，增进了我们对死亡肿瘤细胞如何启动适应性免疫反应的理解，并提供了增强该通路的治疗靶点。
